elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 7(a) as rendered caps both sides: "CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM." The Excluded Claims exception is expressly "UNCAPPED FOR EITHER PARTY".

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered cap is only "THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — no USD 1,000,000 alternative floor and "paid" only, not "paid or payable".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 7(b): "NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" includes "ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS", and Excluded Claims are uncapped for either party.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The Excluded Claims definition lists only indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out.
"EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ..." and Excluded Claims are uncapped for either party; the prior dangling "PARAGRAPH 9" pointer is replaced.
Excluded Claims include "ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT".
Excluded Claims include "GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT".
Fraud does not appear in the Excluded Claims definition or elsewhere in 7(a).

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the Excluded Claims definition; only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Company's cap remains an unqualified "MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT"; no language stating Company's obligation to pay fees is not damages subject to the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Both the Contractor sentence and the Company sentence in 7(a) impose caps, and the Excluded Claims exception is stated to be uncapped for either party.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Both caps now read "THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM", replacing the original open-ended "FEES PAID ... FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES" basis.
Excluded Claims (uncapped for either party) expressly include "A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS"; the defect the finding identified (dangling Paragraph 9 reference) is cured.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" sits within the uncapped Excluded Claims definition.
"ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" is within Excluded Claims, which are uncapped for either party.
Willful misconduct is expressly named in the uncapped Excluded Claims definition.

reasons: Finding status 'deviation' is correct: the original 7(a) capped both parties at total fees paid for the relevant Services with the sole exception pointing at 'PARAGRAPH 9', which is not an indemnification provision, so no usable carve-out existed and indemnification/confidentiality/gross negligence/willful misconduct all sat inside the cap — a fallback failure on carve-outs and on the fee basis.

Fallback is complete as rendered: mutual caps, both restated to fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, plus a mutual, expressly uncapped Excluded Claims definition covering indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct.

Preferred is not reached — no USD 1,000,000 alternative floor, 'paid' rather than 'paid or payable', and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or IP infringement, and no statement that Company's payment obligations are outside the cap. These are correctly acknowledged in the rationale as not pressed.

Minimality defect: the edit deleted the existing Customer-favourable exception 'EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF' rather than preserving it alongside the new carve-outs. Paragraph 9 imposes obligations on Contractor, and removing its uncapped status narrows Customer's protection in a way no selected element requires. Repair: render the opener as 'EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF AND EXCLUDED CLAIMS, WHICH ARE UNCAPPED FOR EITHER PARTY, ...'.

Intent is preserved otherwise: 7(b)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the Statement-of-Work scoping of Contractor's cap, and all commercial mechanics survive; the edit removes rather than creates a dangling cross-reference, and no retained sentence contradicts the new Excluded Claims definition.

Drafting note (not a defect at fallback): Contractor's cap remains scoped to liability 'RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK' while Company's is 'FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT'; this asymmetry favours Customer on scope and need not be changed, but the comment should not describe the caps as identical.
